comment: Spec 058 section 13.1. Every diagnostic the fabric CLI (FC-), the SDKs (FW-), the host emitter (FE-), the reader (FR-) and the Node (FN-) emit, with a stable id, a fixed text, a fix and a docs anchor. Texts and fixes carry no interpolated value: a host name, path or variable value appears only in local output (status files, CLI output), never on telemetry. Each id's docs anchor is its lowercase id in the docs page. Ids are never reused; a retired id stays listed with retired: true.

messages.name: capture_not_installed
messages.text: wire capture is not installed: the configuration is invalid
messages.fix: run `python -m fabric.wire status` with the agent's environment; it names the setting and the fix

messages.name: no_destination
messages.text: spans have no destination: no OTLP endpoint is set, so captured spans are dropped
messages.fix: set FABRIC_OTLP_ENDPOINT (or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT) to the Fabric Node, for example http://127.0.0.1:4318 for a local Node

messages.name: no_store
messages.text: no content store is configured: capture is metadata only, request and response bodies are not kept
messages.fix: set FABRIC_WIRE_STORE=node with FABRIC_WIRE_CONTENT_ENDPOINT, or FABRIC_WIRE_STORE=file:///absolute/dir for a local trial

messages.name: redacted_roles
messages.text: the capture policy masks some content roles and the autoload has no transformation for them: their content is withheld
messages.fix: give those roles retain_original or metadata_only in the capture policy, or install in code with transformations= and FABRIC_REDACTION_ENDPOINT

messages.name: endpoint_set
messages.text: the model endpoints recorded by this process
messages.fix: add a host with FABRIC_WIRE_ENDPOINTS, or pin the built-in rows of an earlier release with FABRIC_WIRE_BUILTIN_ENDPOINTS=legacy

messages.name: unmatched_model_host
messages.text: a model-looking request matched no configured endpoint and was not recorded
messages.fix: add the host to FABRIC_WIRE_ENDPOINTS; the status lists the exact value for each host

messages.name: otel_sdk_disabled
messages.text: capture is disabled by OTEL_SDK_DISABLED: nothing is recorded
messages.fix: unset OTEL_SDK_DISABLED in the agent's environment

messages.name: content_capture_disabled
messages.text: content capture is disabled for this profile; metadata capture continues
messages.fix: the status names the reason; give the production profile a capture policy, an id key and a spool key, or use the local profile

messages.name: spool_backlog
messages.text: records wait in the spool and no process is draining it
messages.fix: run `python -m fabric.wire drain --until-empty` with the agent's environment; for batch or serverless workers set FABRIC_WIRE_DRAIN_ON_EXIT_S

messages.name: otlp_url_credentials
messages.text: an endpoint URL carries credentials, a query or a fragment
messages.fix: remove user:password@, ?query and #fragment from the URL; send credentials as headers (FABRIC_OTLP_HEADERS_FILE or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS)

messages.name: otlp_exporter_missing
messages.text: the OTLP exporter package is not installed
messages.fix: pip install "singleaxis-fabric[otlp]" in the agent's environment

messages.name: otlp_plaintext_non_loopback
messages.text: the OTLP endpoint uses http to a non-loopback host
messages.fix: use https with FABRIC_OTLP_CERTIFICATE (or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE), or a loopback address (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1])

messages.name: otlp_endpoint_missing
messages.text: this delivery mode needs an OTLP traces endpoint
messages.fix: set FABRIC_OTLP_ENDPOINT (or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT) to the Fabric Node, for example http://127.0.0.1:4318 for a local Node

messages.name: endpoints_invalid_json
messages.text: FABRIC_WIRE_ENDPOINTS is not a JSON array of matcher objects
messages.fix: use a JSON array such as [{"endpoint_id":"my-model","dialect":"openai","hosts":["models.example.com"]}]

messages.name: endpoint_matcher_invalid
messages.text: an endpoint matcher is invalid
messages.fix: each entry needs an endpoint_id and provider_name of lowercase letters, digits and ._-, dialect openai or anthropic, hosts or host_suffixes, schemes http/https and ports 1-65535

messages.name: protected_global_provider
messages.text: a Fabric-protected global tracer provider cannot carry wire spans
messages.fix: set FABRIC_OTLP_ENDPOINT (or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT): capture then delivers through its own private tracer provider

messages.name: fabric_otlp_without_endpoint
messages.text: a FABRIC_OTLP_* setting is set without FABRIC_OTLP_ENDPOINT
messages.fix: set FABRIC_OTLP_ENDPOINT, or remove the other FABRIC_OTLP_* variables

messages.name: key_value_and_file
messages.text: a key is set both as a value and as a file
messages.fix: set either the variable or its _FILE variant, not both

messages.name: secret_file_unreadable
messages.text: a key, certificate or headers file is missing, unreadable or malformed
messages.fix: check the path and the permissions of the file the reason names

messages.name: builtin_endpoints_invalid
messages.text: FABRIC_WIRE_BUILTIN_ENDPOINTS has an unknown value
messages.fix: use table (the default: every qualified built-in row) or legacy (the three rows of releases before 0.13)

messages.name: llm_content_ignored
messages.text: FABRIC_CAPTURE_LLM_CONTENT does not affect wire capture
messages.fix: remove FABRIC_CAPTURE_LLM_CONTENT; wire capture keeps content off telemetry in the content store

messages.name: spool_migration_ignored
messages.text: spool plaintext migration is ignored in the production profile; plaintext spool records are quarantined
messages.fix: remove FABRIC_WIRE_SPOOL_MIGRATE_PLAINTEXT, or migrate under the local profile first

messages.name: status_file_unwritable
messages.text: the status file could not be written
messages.fix: point FABRIC_WIRE_STATUS_FILE at a writable path in a directory that exists

messages.name: otlp_setting_invalid
messages.text: an OTLP setting is malformed
messages.fix: headers are k=v pairs separated by commas, timeouts are numbers, compression is gzip, deflate or none, and a client key and certificate are set together

messages.name: config_not_found
messages.text: no fabric.yaml was found
messages.fix: create fabric.yaml (schema: fabric.config/v1) in the project directory, or pass --config PATH

messages.name: config_unreadable
messages.text: fabric.yaml could not be read or is not valid YAML
messages.fix: check the file; the message names the line and column

messages.name: config_unknown_key
messages.text: fabric.yaml has a key the schema does not know
messages.fix: remove the key or use the suggested one; the schema is contracts/cli-config/v1/fabric-config-v1.schema.json

messages.name: config_invalid_value
messages.text: a fabric.yaml value is not allowed
messages.fix: use one of the values the message lists

messages.name: cli_extra_missing
messages.text: this command needs the [cli] extra
messages.fix: pip install "singleaxis-fabric[cli]" (or pipx install "singleaxis-fabric[cli]")

messages.name: unknown_command
messages.text: unknown command
messages.fix: run `fabric help` for the list of commands

messages.name: config_schema_unsupported
messages.text: fabric.yaml names a schema this CLI does not support
messages.fix: set schema: fabric.config/v1, or upgrade the CLI

messages.name: provider_url_invalid
messages.text: a provider URL is not a usable model endpoint
messages.fix: give the base URL the client uses, such as https://my-llm.example.com/v1, optionally prefixed anthropic= for the Anthropic dialect

messages.name: env_overrides_config
messages.text: an environment variable overrides a fabric.yaml setting
messages.fix: unset the variable if fabric.yaml should decide

messages.name: command_not_built
messages.text: this command is not part of this release yet
messages.fix: upgrade the CLI; until then follow docs/reference/manual-setup/quickstart.md

messages.name: option_not_built
messages.text: this option is not part of this release yet
messages.fix: use the local profile's defaults; production, Kubernetes and the other destinations follow docs/reference/manual-setup/production-setup.md and docs/reference/manual-setup/deployment.md until the CLI builds them

messages.name: secrets_dir_unsafe
messages.text: the secrets directory is not a private directory of this user
messages.fix: make it a real directory you own with mode 0700 (chmod 700 DIR), or set secrets.dir in fabric.yaml to another path

messages.name: secret_file_unsafe
messages.text: a secret file is a symlink, is not a regular file, or is open to other users
messages.fix: restore it as your own regular file with mode 0600 (chmod 600 FILE), or replace it with `fabric init --rotate NAME`

messages.name: secret_set_incomplete
messages.text: a generated certificate is missing its key or its CA
messages.fix: run `fabric init --rotate ca` to issue a new CA and Node certificate, then `fabric up` and restart agents

messages.name: rotation_needs_restart
messages.text: a rotated secret is still in use by running processes
messages.fix: run `fabric up` so the Node restarts with it; restart agents when the CA or the id key changed

messages.name: config_secret_shaped
messages.text: fabric.yaml must not hold a secret value
messages.fix: put the value in a file and name the file's path (start a relative path with ./); `fabric init` generates and stores secrets itself

messages.name: env_not_imported
messages.text: an environment setting could not be written into fabric.yaml
messages.fix: keep exporting the variable (a variable already set wins over fabric.yaml), or pass --import-secrets to store a key given by value as a file

messages.name: docker_missing
messages.text: Docker with Compose v2 is not installed or not on PATH
messages.fix: install Docker Engine or Docker Desktop (the `docker compose` plugin included), then run the command again

messages.name: docker_not_running
messages.text: the Docker daemon did not answer
messages.fix: start Docker Desktop or the docker service and check `docker info`; on Linux add your user to the docker group or use sudo

messages.name: compose_failed
messages.text: Docker Compose could not apply the Fabric project
messages.fix: read the detail (Docker's own last lines); `docker compose -p fabric-PROJECT logs` shows the services' output

messages.name: port_in_use
messages.text: the Node's port is already in use on this machine
messages.fix: stop the other listener (an earlier local stack: `fabric down` in that project, or `make down` in deploy/compose), or set node.endpoint: https://localhost:PORT in fabric.yaml and run `fabric up` again

messages.name: node_not_healthy
messages.text: the Fabric Node did not answer over TLS in time
messages.fix: run `fabric up --wait 180` to allow a slow first image pull; the detail holds the Node's last log line

messages.name: node_external
messages.text: node.mode is external: there is nothing for this command to start or stop
messages.fix: nothing to do; set node.mode: docker in fabric.yaml to have `fabric up` run a local Node

messages.name: certificate_renewed
messages.text: the Node certificate was close to expiry and was reissued from the local CA
messages.fix: nothing to do: agents trust the CA, which did not change

messages.name: project_changed
messages.text: the running project differed from fabric.yaml or this CLI's pinned images and was updated
messages.fix: nothing to do; the detail names what changed

messages.name: ca_expired
messages.text: the local CA has expired
messages.fix: run `fabric init --rotate ca`, then `fabric up`, then restart agents so they load the new CA

messages.name: image_override
messages.text: an environment variable replaces an image pinned by this CLI release
messages.fix: unset the variable to run the pinned, signed release image; keep it only to test a locally built image

messages.name: state_not_removed
messages.text: part of the project's local state could not be removed
messages.fix: remove the directory named in the detail by hand (files written by a container running as root need sudo)

messages.name: compose_project_not_this_projects
messages.text: the Compose project this command would act on holds containers of another project, so nothing was started, stopped or removed
messages.fix: two projects with the same name share one Compose project: set a different `project:` in this directory's fabric.yaml and run the command again, or run `fabric down` in the directory named in the detail first

messages.name: referenced_secret_unreadable
messages.text: a secret file fabric.yaml references is missing or not a readable regular file, so agents given the compiled environment would capture nothing with it
messages.fix: correct the path in fabric.yaml (secrets.id_key_file or secrets.ca_file) and run `fabric init` again, or remove the setting so `fabric init` generates the secret

messages.name: project_flag_not_the_files
messages.text: --project names another project than the fabric.yaml this command found, so nothing was done
messages.fix: drop --project (fabric.yaml names the project), pass --config with that project's fabric.yaml, or rename this project with `fabric down` and then `fabric init --project NAME`

messages.name: sensor_started
messages.text: the host sensor is running and scoped to this project's agent cgroup
messages.fix: start the agent with `fabric run -- CMD`, which joins this cgroup on Linux; a process started another way is outside the sensor's scope unless its shell joins first (`echo $$ | sudo tee DETAIL/cgroup.procs`)

messages.name: sensor_off
messages.text: the host sensor is off by configuration
messages.fix: set sensor.kind: auto in fabric.yaml and drop --no-sensor to start it where it can load

messages.name: sensor_desktop_vm
messages.text: the host sensor runs inside the Docker VM: it cannot see a process started directly on this machine
messages.fix: nothing to do for capture from the SDK, which is unaffected; for independent host evidence run the agent on a Linux host

messages.name: sensor_kernel_unsupported
messages.text: this kernel cannot load the eBPF sensor (it needs Linux 5.8 or later with BTF and cgroup v2)
messages.fix: use a host with a newer kernel; capture from the SDK is unaffected, only independent host evidence is missing

messages.name: sensor_cgroup_not_permitted
messages.text: the agent cgroup for the host sensor could not be created
messages.fix: run `fabric up` once with sudo, or from a systemd user session (a delegated cgroup); capture from the SDK is unaffected

messages.name: sensor_start_failed
messages.text: the host sensor container did not stay running
messages.fix: read the detail (the sensor's last log line); `fabric up --no-sensor` continues without host evidence

messages.name: sensor_auditd_available
messages.text: eBPF cannot load here but auditd is present on this host
messages.fix: follow docs/reference/host-sensors.md to run the auditd sensor collector; the CLI does not start it in this release

messages.name: sensor_sandboxed_runtime
messages.text: this machine runs inside a sandbox or container that hides the host kernel from the sensor
messages.fix: run `fabric up` on the host itself for host evidence; capture from the SDK is unaffected

messages.name: node_not_started
messages.text: `fabric up` has not started this project's local Node, so the agent's records wait in its spool
messages.fix: run `fabric up`; the spool delivers the records once the Node answers

messages.name: sdk_version_skew
messages.text: the agent's SDK and this CLI are more than one minor version apart
messages.fix: upgrade the older one so both come from the same release (pip install -U "singleaxis-fabric[otlp]" in the agent's environment, or upgrade the CLI)

messages.name: run_sdk_missing
messages.text: the agent's Python interpreter cannot load the Fabric SDK, so this run is not captured; the agent ran unchanged
messages.fix: install the SDK in the agent's own environment with the command in the detail (python -m pip install "singleaxis-fabric[otlp]" with that interpreter), then start the agent again

messages.name: run_otlp_exporter_missing
messages.text: the agent's environment has the Fabric SDK but not the OTLP exporter that sends records to the Node, so this run is not captured; the agent ran unchanged
messages.fix: install the [otlp] extra in the agent's environment with the command in the detail, then start the agent again

messages.name: run_config_unusable
messages.text: the project's configuration could not be used, so the agent ran without capture
messages.fix: run `fabric doctor` in the project directory: it names the problem and its fix (the detail names the first one)

messages.name: run_env_only
messages.text: this command is not a Python program `fabric run` can turn capture on for; it was given the run's Fabric settings only
messages.fix: start a Python agent through its interpreter (fabric run -- python app.py) or the project's .venv; a launcher script can export `fabric run --print-env` itself; Node.js and compiled agents record through the explicit API and the host sensor

messages.name: run_cgroup_join_failed
messages.text: the agent could not join the host sensor's cgroup, so the sensor does not observe this run
messages.fix: start the agent as the user that ran `fabric up`, or run `fabric up` from a systemd user session (a delegated cgroup); capture by the SDK is unaffected

messages.name: run_command_not_found
messages.text: the agent command could not be started
messages.fix: check the command name, that it is on PATH and that it is executable; the detail names it

messages.name: run_no_command
messages.text: `fabric run` needs the agent command after --
messages.fix: fabric run -- python agent.py

messages.name: run_state_unwritable
messages.text: the run could not be recorded under .fabric/state, so it ran without capture and `fabric verify` and `fabric show` do not see it
messages.fix: make the project's .fabric directory a real directory writable by this user (not a symlink), then start the agent again

messages.name: run_capture_off_by_flag
messages.text: capture is off for this run (--no-capture): the agent ran with its environment unchanged
messages.fix: drop --no-capture to record the run

messages.name: run_label_invalid
messages.text: the --run label is not usable, so a generated label was used
messages.fix: use 1-64 letters, digits and ._- for --run

messages.name: compiled_env_stale
messages.text: .fabric/compiled.env is missing or was made from an older fabric.yaml
messages.fix: run `fabric init` (or `fabric up`) to rewrite it; `fabric run` compiles fabric.yaml itself and is not affected, launchers that read the file are

messages.name: node_unreachable
messages.text: the Fabric Node did not answer over TLS with the project's CA
messages.fix: run `fabric up`; if it is running, `fabric doctor` prints its last log line (docker compose -p fabric-PROJECT logs fabric-node shows more)

messages.name: canary_not_captured
messages.text: the canary could not record a model exchange with this project's configuration
messages.fix: the detail holds the SDK's reason and fix; `fabric doctor` checks the same configuration

messages.name: canary_not_delivered
messages.text: the canary's records did not reach the destination in time
messages.fix: check that the Node runs (`fabric up`) and answers (`fabric doctor`); on a slow machine allow more time with fabric verify --wait 120

messages.name: canary_incomplete
messages.text: the canary run was read back but is not complete
messages.fix: each reason in the detail names its fix; python -m fabric.reconstruct --spans DATA/spans --run LABEL prints the full report

messages.name: canary_complete
messages.text: the canary went through capture, the Node and the destination and was read back complete
messages.fix: nothing to do

messages.name: no_run_recorded
messages.text: no `fabric run` is recorded in this project yet, so only the path was checked
messages.fix: start the agent with `fabric run -- CMD`, then run `fabric verify` again

messages.name: run_not_found
messages.text: the run's records were not found in the destination
messages.fix: check the label (`fabric show --list`); a run still in progress or just ended may not be delivered yet: run the command again after the agent exits

messages.name: run_incomplete
messages.text: the run's records are not complete in the reader's verdict
messages.fix: each reason in the detail names its fix; `fabric show` displays what was recorded

messages.name: run_complete
messages.text: the run's records were read back complete and its model decisions were recorded
messages.fix: nothing to do

messages.name: run_not_captured
messages.text: the run was started without capture
messages.fix: the detail lists the reasons recorded when it started; `fabric doctor` shows each with its fix

messages.name: records_unreadable
messages.text: the destination's span files could not be read
messages.fix: the detail names the input and the accepted forms; check the destination directory

messages.name: destination_not_readable
messages.text: this destination is not one Fabric can read back, so records were checked only up to the Node
messages.fix: pass --spans PATH with an export of the destination's spans, or use the local-dir destination

messages.name: no_runs
messages.text: no `fabric run` is recorded in this project
messages.fix: start the agent with `fabric run -- CMD`

messages.name: content_hidden
messages.text: content is not printed because stdout is not a terminal
messages.fix: pass --content to print it

messages.name: manual_setup
messages.text: no fabric.yaml was found: checking this shell's FABRIC_* environment as a manual setup
messages.fix: nothing to do for a manual setup; `fabric init --from-env` writes fabric.yaml from it

messages.name: sdk_ready
messages.text: the agent's Python environment loads the Fabric SDK with this project's settings and reports no problem
messages.fix: nothing to do

messages.name: other_fabric_on_path
messages.text: another program named fabric comes first on PATH
messages.fix: use the singleaxis-fabric command, which is always this CLI, or put this CLI's directory first on PATH

messages.name: sensor_stopped
messages.text: `fabric up` started the host sensor, but its container is not running now
messages.fix: run `fabric up` again; the detail holds the sensor's last log line

messages.name: node_ok
messages.text: the Fabric Node answers over TLS with the project's CA
messages.fix: nothing to do

messages.name: no_status_file
messages.text: the last run left no status file: its agent never loaded the SDK, or was stopped before it started
messages.fix: start the agent with `fabric run` again; if this repeats, the agent's interpreter is not the one with the SDK (`fabric doctor` names the one it checked)

messages.name: no_problem_found
messages.text: no problem found
messages.fix: nothing to do

messages.name: launcher_command_unavailable
messages.text: the npm launcher has the `run` and `doctor` commands only; this command is in the Python CLI and the fabric-cli container image
messages.fix: install the full CLI with pipx install "singleaxis-fabric[cli]" (or uv tool install), or run the image: docker run --rm -it -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock -v "$PWD:$PWD" -w "$PWD" ghcr.io/singleaxis/fabric-cli:VERSION COMMAND

messages.name: doctor_no_python
messages.text: no Python interpreter was found, so the Python SDK check was skipped
messages.fix: nothing to do for a Node.js agent, which records through the explicit API; for a Python agent, put its interpreter on PATH or create the project's .venv and run `fabric doctor` again

messages.name: kubectl_missing
messages.text: kubectl is not installed or not on PATH, so the Secrets cannot be written to the cluster
messages.fix: install kubectl and select the cluster's context (kubectl config use-context NAME), or write the Secrets as manifests with `fabric init --kubernetes --render DIR` and apply them with your own tooling

messages.name: kube_namespace_missing
messages.text: a namespace the Secrets belong in does not exist
messages.fix: create it (kubectl create namespace NAME) and run the command again; neither the chart's secrets Job nor `fabric init --kubernetes` creates a namespace

messages.name: kube_forbidden
messages.text: the Kubernetes API refused the request: the identity may not read or create Secrets there
messages.fix: use a kube context that may get and create Secrets in the release namespace and every agent namespace; for the chart's secrets Job, check that every agent namespace is listed in agentNamespaces (its Role is created there)

messages.name: kube_api_unreachable
messages.text: the Kubernetes API server could not be reached
messages.fix: check the kube context (kubectl cluster-info); in the chart's secrets Job, check that a NetworkPolicy lets the Job reach the API server (set secretsJob.apiServer.to and .ports when the chart cannot read them)

messages.name: kube_secret_incomplete
messages.text: an existing Secret lacks keys this setup needs; it is kept unchanged
messages.fix: delete the Secret the message names and run the command again to generate it (a new id key changes the namespace's pseudonyms), or add the missing keys it lists yourself

messages.name: kube_ingress_secret_orphaned
messages.text: an agent namespace's ingress Secret exists in the release namespace but its agent Secret does not, so a new token and source id would not match it
messages.fix: delete the ingress Secret the message names (kubectl delete secret -n RELEASE-NAMESPACE NAME) and run the command again; both are then generated together

messages.name: kube_option_needs_kubernetes
messages.text: this option belongs to `fabric init --kubernetes`
messages.fix: add --kubernetes, or remove the option

messages.name: injector_ca_bundle
messages.text: the injector's webhook needs the CA certificate as its caBundle
messages.fix: the chart's secrets Job sets it; with secretsJob.enabled=false, set injector.caBundle to the ca.crt entry of the CA Secret's data, which is base64 already (kubectl get secret fabric-ca -n RELEASE-NAMESPACE -o yaml)

messages.name: kube_webhook_missing
messages.text: the injector's webhook configuration was not found, so its caBundle cannot be set
messages.fix: install or upgrade the chart with injector.enabled=true first; the post-install hook then sets the caBundle

messages.name: kube_name_invalid
messages.text: a namespace, release, source or Secret name is not valid for Kubernetes
messages.fix: use lowercase letters, digits and '-' (at most 63 characters for a namespace); a source label may also use '.', '_' and ':'

messages.name: kube_agent_secret_unusable
messages.text: an agent namespace's existing Secret holds no ingest credential or id key this setup can read, so the namespace's ingress Secret cannot be made and the Node, which reads it, would not start
messages.fix: delete the agent Secret the message names (kubectl delete secret -n AGENT-NAMESPACE NAME) and run the command again, or run helm upgrade again; the agent Secret and its ingress Secret are then generated together (a new id key changes the namespace's pseudonyms; restart its agents)

messages.name: kube_certificate_expiring
messages.text: a certificate in a Secret expires within 14 days; Secrets are never overwritten, so it is not renewed by itself
messages.fix: delete the Node's or injector's Secret the message names and rerun the command (helm upgrade runs the secrets Job): a new certificate comes from the same CA; restart the Node if it was its own. For an agent or CA Secret see 'Certificate renewal' in docs/reference/manual-setup/deployment.md

messages.name: kube_certificate_expired
messages.text: a certificate in a Secret has expired, so the connections it secures fail: agents cannot deliver to the Node, or the injector's webhook is skipped and pods start without capture
messages.fix: delete the Node's or injector's Secret the message names and rerun the command (helm upgrade runs the secrets Job): a new certificate comes from the same CA; restart the Node if it was its own. For an agent or CA Secret see 'Certificate renewal' in docs/reference/manual-setup/deployment.md

messages.name: kube_host_sensor_needs_production
messages.text: the host sensor's Secrets need a production Node: each node's sensor is an authenticated source with its own ingress group
messages.fix: add --profile production (the chart: preset=production-host-sensor), or leave --host-sensor out

messages.name: kube_host_source_id_stale
messages.text: a node's host sensor Secret holds a source id made with another id key, so the Node would refuse that sensor's records
messages.fix: delete the node's Secret the message names (kubectl delete secret -n RELEASE-NAMESPACE NAME) and run the command again (or helm upgrade): it is made again from the current id key; then restart the Node

messages.name: kube_agent_id_key_differs
messages.text: an agent namespace's Secret holds an id key of its own, not the release's shared one, so host sensor records do not join that namespace's runs
messages.fix: delete the agent Secret and its ingress Secret the message names and run the command again (or helm upgrade): both are made again with the shared id key; then restart that namespace's agents

messages.name: kubectl_missing_for_read
messages.text: kubectl is not installed or not on PATH; --kubernetes reads the cluster of the current kube context through it
messages.fix: install kubectl and select the cluster's context (kubectl config use-context NAME), or point KUBECONFIG at its file

messages.name: helm_missing
messages.text: helm is not installed or not on PATH; `fabric up --kubernetes` installs the chart with it
messages.fix: install Helm 3.14 or later, or write the values and Secrets for your own pipeline with fabric up --kubernetes --render DIR

messages.name: kube_release_not_found
messages.text: no Fabric release installed with a preset was found in the cluster of the current kube context
messages.fix: install it (fabric up --kubernetes, or helm install with --set preset=...); name its namespace with --namespace when it is not fabric-system; check the context with kubectl config current-context

messages.name: helm_failed
messages.text: Helm could not install or remove the Fabric release
messages.fix: read the detail (Helm's own last lines); a chart error names the value and its fix, and `fabric doctor --kubernetes` shows the state of what is installed

messages.name: kube_release_applied
messages.text: the Fabric release was installed or upgraded with Helm; no workload other than Fabric's own was restarted
messages.fix: nothing to do; agent pods get capture at their next start, by your own rollout

messages.name: kube_secret_missing
messages.text: a Secret the release needs is missing or lacks a key, so the pods that mount it do not start or cannot authenticate
messages.fix: run helm upgrade (the secrets Job makes each missing Secret) or fabric init --kubernetes with the same namespaces; an incomplete Secret is never changed: delete it first

messages.name: kube_node_not_ready
messages.text: the Fabric Node has no ready pod, so no record is accepted
messages.fix: the detail holds the pod's state and last log line; kubectl describe pod and kubectl logs in the release namespace show more

messages.name: kube_node_ready
messages.text: the Fabric Node's pods are ready and its health endpoint answers
messages.fix: nothing to do

messages.name: kube_port_forward_failed
messages.text: kubectl could not forward a local port to the Fabric Node
messages.fix: check that the Node's pods run and that your identity may create pods/portforward in the release namespace

messages.name: kube_injector_unavailable
messages.text: the pod injector has no ready pod: annotated pods are admitted unchanged after the 2 second webhook timeout and run without capture
messages.fix: restore it (kubectl describe deployment in the release namespace shows why it is down), then recreate the affected pods with your own rollout; Fabric never restarts a workload

messages.name: kube_pod_not_injected
messages.text: a pod asks for injection with the fabric.singleaxis.ai/inject annotation but was not injected, so it runs without capture
messages.fix: the detail says why; fix that, then recreate the pod with your own rollout: injection happens only when a pod is created

messages.name: kube_pods_injected
messages.text: annotated pods in the agent namespaces carry the injected annotation
messages.fix: nothing to do

messages.name: kube_namespace_not_labelled
messages.text: an agent namespace lacks the label fabric.singleaxis.ai/injection=enabled, so the injector never sees its pods
messages.fix: kubectl label namespace NAME fabric.singleaxis.ai/injection=enabled, then recreate its annotated pods with your own rollout

messages.name: kube_sensor_not_running
messages.text: the host sensor is not running on a node it was installed for, so no host evidence is recorded there
messages.fix: the detail holds the pod's state and last log line; a node without Linux 5.8 and BTF cannot run it: keep it off such nodes with hostSensor.nodeSelector

messages.name: kube_pods_unscoped
messages.text: the host sensor selected pods it cannot observe; the detail gives the node, the count and the reason
messages.fix: cgroup_not_found: set EMIT_AGENT_CGROUP_ROOTS through hostSensor.env; unsupported_runtime (gVisor, Kata): rely on wire capture for that pod or use the default runtime; pod_limit: narrow hostSensor.agentPodSelector

messages.name: kube_sensor_export_failing
messages.text: a host sensor cannot deliver its records to the Fabric Node; the detail holds the gRPC status code
messages.fix: Unavailable: the Node is down or a NetworkPolicy blocks the sensor (keep networkPolicy.hostSensorEgress on); Unauthenticated or PermissionDenied: run helm upgrade so the node's Secret and ingress group agree

messages.name: kube_sensor_scoped
messages.text: the host sensor runs and reports the agent pods it observes on each node
messages.fix: nothing to do

messages.name: kube_network_policy_blocks
messages.text: a NetworkPolicy selects Fabric's pods and no rule of the chart allows the traffic the detail names
messages.fix: keep the chart's own policies on (otel-collector.networkPolicy.enabled, hostSensorEgress); for a policy of your own add an allow rule from the pods named to the Node's ingress port

messages.name: kube_runtime_class_unsupported
messages.text: a RuntimeClass of this cluster uses gVisor or Kata: the host sensor cannot observe pods that run under it
messages.fix: nothing to change for pods on the default runtime; for a pod under that RuntimeClass rely on wire capture in the agent (the injector), and expect no host evidence

messages.name: kube_node_without_sensor
messages.text: a node cannot run the host sensor or is not in the release's node list, so pods on it have no host evidence
messages.fix: a serverless, virtual or non-Linux node cannot run it: rely on wire capture there; for a node added after the install run helm upgrade so it gets its Secret and ingress group

messages.name: kube_spool_emptydir_one_shot
messages.text: a pod that runs once (a Job, or restartPolicy Never) has an emptyDir spool: records not delivered when it exits are lost with the pod
messages.fix: raise FABRIC_WIRE_DRAIN_ON_EXIT_S for it (injector.env), or give it a persistent spool with the annotation fabric.singleaxis.ai/spool: pvc

messages.name: kube_run_not_corroborated
messages.text: the host sensor is installed but no host record joined this run, so nothing independent of the agent corroborates it
messages.fix: check that the pod carries the sensor's pod label (the injector adds it) and FABRIC_HOST_LABEL, and that `fabric doctor --kubernetes` shows the pod scoped on its node

messages.name: kube_canary_needs_binding
messages.text: the canary was not sent: on a production Node every source has its own ingress binding, and this release generates none for the canary
messages.fix: nothing to do; the run's own records are read instead (pass --spans PATH with your destination's export)

messages.name: kube_rendered
messages.text: the Helm values and the Secret manifests were written for your own pipeline; nothing was installed
messages.fix: apply the Secrets first (kubectl create -f DIR/secrets --recursive), then helm upgrade --install with the values file; encrypt the manifests before they reach a repository

messages.name: kube_purged
messages.text: the release was removed and the Secrets Fabric generated for it were deleted
messages.fix: nothing to do; an agent pod that still runs keeps the files it mounted until it stops

messages.name: kube_webhook_ca_missing
messages.text: the injector's webhook has no caBundle, so the API server cannot verify it and admits annotated pods unchanged
messages.fix: run helm upgrade (its post-upgrade Job sets the caBundle from the generated CA), or set injector.caBundle to the base64 of the CA certificate

messages.name: kube_no_agent_namespace
messages.text: the release serves no agent namespace, so no agent pod can deliver records to this Node
messages.fix: name the namespaces of your agents: helm upgrade with --set agentNamespaces=NS (or fabric up --kubernetes --agent-namespace NS)

messages.name: kube_api_forbidden_read
messages.text: the identity of the kube context may not read something this check needs, so that part was skipped
messages.fix: the detail names what; ask for get and list on it, or run the command with an identity that may read the release namespace and the nodes

messages.name: kube_plan_ready
messages.text: the cluster was read; nothing was changed
messages.fix: follow the next command the plan prints

messages.name: kube_released_secrets_kept
messages.text: the release was removed; the Secrets Fabric generated are kept, so a new install keeps every key and id
messages.fix: nothing to do; fabric down --kubernetes --purge deletes them too

messages.name: kube_host_nodes_needed
messages.text: the host sensor needs the names of the nodes it runs on, and they could not be read from the cluster of the current kube context
messages.fix: pass --host-node NAME for each node that runs the sensor, oldest first (kubectl get nodes --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp)

messages.name: kube_option_invalid
messages.text: an option given with --kubernetes cannot be used as given; nothing was installed or changed
messages.fix: the detail names the option and what it takes; `fabric help up` lists the options

messages.name: chart_override
messages.text: FABRIC_CHART replaces the chart of this CLI release, so the chart installed is not the one this release pins
messages.fix: unset FABRIC_CHART to install this release's own chart; keep it only to test a chart under development

messages.name: content_reader_missing
messages.text: the release delivers model bodies to an S3 content store, and reading them back needs boto3, which this CLI install lacks
messages.fix: pip install "singleaxis-fabric[cli,s3]" on this workstation, then run fabric verify --kubernetes again

messages.name: content_not_readable
messages.text: the release keeps no model bodies where this workstation can read them, so the agent's model decisions cannot be verified and verify cannot pass
messages.fix: deliver content to an S3 or S3-compatible store: otel-collector.content.enabled=true and content.backend=s3 in your values (docs/get-started/kubernetes.md); this workstation reads it with your AWS configuration

messages.name: no_capture_policy
messages.text: the injector gives agents no capture policy, so on this production Node they record metadata only: the model bodies the agent's decisions are verified against are never kept and verify cannot pass
messages.fix: set injector.capturePolicy to your fabric.deployment-policy/v1 document in your values (docs/get-started/kubernetes.md), run fabric up --kubernetes again, then roll out your agents

messages.name: sensor_runtime_class_unread
messages.text: the host sensor could not read the RuntimeClass of some selected pods, so a gVisor or Kata pod among them cannot be reported unsupported_runtime and may be counted as scoped
messages.fix: grant the sensor's service account get on runtimeclasses.node.k8s.io (the chart's ClusterRole does: run helm upgrade; for deploy/kubernetes/host-emitter-daemonset.yaml apply its current ClusterRole), and check that each RuntimeClass the pods name exists

messages.name: plan_ready
messages.text: this machine and the agent were read; nothing was changed, started or contacted
messages.fix: follow the next command the plan prints; each fix row names the command that closes its gap

messages.name: plan_sdk_missing
messages.text: the agent's interpreter does not have the Fabric SDK yet, so nothing is recorded until it does
messages.fix: install it in the agent's own environment with the command in the detail (the plan's next line starts with it)

messages.name: plan_packages_unread
messages.text: the agent's installed packages could not be listed, so rows that depend on a library assume it is present
messages.fix: name the agent's interpreter, for example fabric plan -- .venv/bin/python app.py, and check that it starts

messages.name: plan_runtime_unknown
messages.text: the agent's runtime could not be told: no command was given and the directory has no project manifest
messages.fix: give the agent command after --, for example fabric plan -- python app.py

messages.name: plan_mcp_config_unreadable
messages.text: an --mcp-config file is not a JSON object whose mcpServers entries have a command or a url
messages.fix: pass the MCP client's configuration file: an mcpServers object whose entries have a command (a stdio server) or a url (an HTTP server)

messages.name: coverage_prediction_mismatch
messages.text: fabric.yaml turns on a capture point that the run's capture manifest reports off
messages.fix: run fabric doctor for the SDK's reason, and start the agent with fabric run in this project so it gets the setting

messages.name: run_reported_not_verified
messages.text: the run's records were reported by the agent's code through the TypeScript SDK's explicit API, so its model decisions are unsupported(unsupported_runtime): reported, never verified
messages.fix: nothing to fix in the setup: zero-code capture of Node.js model calls is not built yet; fabric show displays the reported records, and the host sensor records the process's connections

messages.name: node_run_nothing_reported
messages.text: no record of this Node.js run reached the destination
messages.fix: build the agent's exporter with new OTLPTraceExporter(fabricExporterOptions()) from @singleaxis/fabric, record each decision with fabric.decision(...), call provider.shutdown() before the process exits, and start the agent with fabric run

messages.name: production_destination_needed
messages.text: the production profile needs a destination that keeps records
messages.fix: choose one with fabric init --production: --destination trial to try the production Node (not durable); or s3 (--bucket NAME --region REGION), s3-compatible (--endpoint URL --bucket NAME) or otlp, each with --otlp-endpoint URL --otlp-headers-file FILE

messages.name: production_policy_missing
messages.text: the production profile needs a capture policy file, and capture.privacy names none or a file that does not exist
messages.fix: run `fabric init --production` to write the production preset (fabric-capture-policy.json) into the project, or set capture.privacy to the path of your own fabric.deployment-policy/v1 file

messages.name: capture_policy_refused
messages.text: the SDK would refuse this capture policy, so agents would keep no content
messages.fix: make it a valid fabric.deployment-policy/v1 document with this project's tenant as tenant_id and deployment.profile production; or move it away and run `fabric init --production` to write the preset again

messages.name: capture_policy_image_placeholder
messages.text: the capture policy names the all-zero placeholder as the agent's image digest
messages.fix: set deployment.image_digest in the policy file to your agent image's digest (the Id that docker image inspect IMAGE prints); a new project takes it as fabric init --production --image-digest sha256:...

messages.name: secret_pair_mismatch
messages.text: a source's token file and its headers file hold different tokens
messages.fix: run `fabric init --rotate tokens` to write a new token and headers file for every source, then `fabric up` and restart agents

messages.name: queue_exceeds_disk
messages.text: node.queue_size is more than the disk under the Node's queue has free, so a long destination outage could fill that disk
messages.fix: set node.queue_size to the size the message names (or auto: half the free space), or free space on that disk; real batches are far smaller than the worst case, so this is advice, not a failure

messages.name: queue_disk_low
messages.text: the disk under the Node's queue has so little free space that the queue holds few batches during a destination outage
messages.fix: free space on that disk or keep the project on a larger one, then run `fabric init` again; agents keep records in their own spool while the Node's queue is full

messages.name: trial_destination
messages.text: the trial destination is not durable storage: it is for trying the production Node before a real destination exists
messages.fix: for real records choose a destination you own: fabric init --destination s3 --bucket NAME --region REGION --otlp-endpoint URL --otlp-headers-file FILE (or s3-compatible, or otlp)

messages.name: no_content_store
messages.text: this production destination keeps no model bodies, so the reader cannot check model decisions against them
messages.fix: to keep content, add an S3 store for it: fabric init --destination s3 --bucket NAME --region REGION --otlp-endpoint URL --otlp-headers-file FILE (spans still go to that OTLP endpoint)

messages.name: destination_file_unusable
messages.text: a file the destination names is missing, unreadable, or open to other users
messages.fix: correct the path in fabric.yaml (destination.ca_file, credentials_file, otlp_ca_file or otlp_headers_file), make it readable by you, chmod 0600 a credentials or headers file, and run `fabric init` again

messages.name: image_digest_not_written
messages.text: --image-digest was not written: the capture policy file already exists, and fabric init never rewrites it
messages.fix: set deployment.image_digest in the policy file the detail names to the digest you passed (the file is yours to edit), then run `fabric init` again to check it

messages.name: export_authorization_missing
messages.text: the span destination is given no Authorization header, so the Node would deliver records unauthenticated
messages.fix: give your collector's headers file, one line Authorization=Bearer%20TOKEN in a 0600 file: `fabric init --otlp-headers-file PATH`, then `fabric up`

messages.name: sensor_id_key_mode
messages.text: the host sensor reads its id key only as a file of mode 0400 or 0440; the referenced id key has another mode, so the sensor stays off
messages.fix: chmod 0400 the id key file the detail names (it stays yours), then run `fabric up` again

messages.name: production_export_endpoint
messages.text: the span destination is not a valid https URL; production egress requires https
messages.fix: set your collector's https:// URL, without user info, query or fragment: `fabric init --otlp-endpoint URL`, then `fabric up`

messages.name: production_token_file
messages.text: an ingress group's token file is missing, not one line of 32 to 4096 printable characters, ends with a newline, or is group-writable or readable by others: the Node would refuse it
messages.fix: run `fabric init` to generate a missing token, or `fabric init --rotate tokens` to replace a bad one (64 hex characters); a token file is one line with no trailing newline, mode 0600

messages.name: production_tokens_shared
messages.text: two ingress groups hold the same token bytes, so one group's sender could present as another's source
messages.fix: give every group its own token: `fabric init --rotate tokens`, then `fabric up`, and restart agents and the sensor

messages.name: production_source_id
messages.text: an ingress group's source id is missing or not an s- pseudonym of 32 hex characters
messages.fix: run `fabric init` again: it derives every source id from the id key and the source labels

messages.name: production_source_ids_shared
messages.text: two ingress groups bind the same source id, so the Node could not tell their records apart
messages.fix: give the agent an id of its own (`fabric init --agent ID`, not the canary's or the sensor's label), then `fabric up`

messages.name: production_tenant
messages.text: the bound tenant id is missing or not a safe id
messages.fix: set the tenant to letters, digits, dot, underscore or dash, at most 128: `fabric init --tenant ID`, then `fabric up`

messages.name: production_receiver_tls
messages.text: an ingress-group listener of the rendered Node configuration serves no TLS
messages.fix: run `fabric up` again to render the Node configuration; never edit .fabric/compose by hand

messages.name: production_content_key
messages.text: the Node content key is missing or does not hold a 32-byte key (raw or base64)
messages.fix: move the bad file aside and run `fabric init` to generate a new content key; content sealed with the old key needs it to be read

messages.name: production_content_store
messages.text: the content store settings are unusable: the bucket name, the region, an https endpoint or server-side encryption (aws:kms or AES256)
messages.fix: correct them with `fabric init --bucket NAME --region REGION` (and `--endpoint https://...` for an S3-compatible store), then `fabric up`

messages.name: production_spool_key
messages.text: the agent's spool key is missing or does not hold a 32-byte key, so the spool cannot be encrypted
messages.fix: move the bad file aside and run `fabric init` to generate a new spool key (records still spooled under the old key are lost)

messages.name: certificate_expires_soon
messages.text: a generated certificate expires within 14 days
messages.fix: run `fabric up` (it renews the Node's and its services' certificates); for client certificates `fabric init --rotate client-certs`, then restart agents and the sensor

messages.name: certificate_expired
messages.text: a generated certificate has expired, so TLS with it fails
messages.fix: run `fabric up` to renew the Node's and its services' certificates, or `fabric init --rotate client-certs` (`--rotate ca` for the CA), then restart agents and the sensor

messages.name: production_node_image_skew
messages.text: the running Fabric Node's image is not the one this CLI release pins
messages.fix: run `fabric up` to apply this release's pinned images (unset FABRIC_NODE_IMAGE unless you are testing your own build)

messages.name: production_sensor_off
messages.text: the host sensor is not running in production mode bound to its own ingress group, so host evidence is not recorded
messages.fix: on Linux with eBPF, run `fabric up` as root or with a delegated cgroup; `fabric doctor` says why the sensor did not start

messages.name: clock_unsynchronized
messages.text: this host's clock is not synchronized, so record times may be off and ordering across hosts uncertain
messages.fix: turn on time synchronization (systemd-timesyncd, chrony or ntpd) and check it with `timedatectl`

messages.name: production_not_started
messages.text: this project's production Node was not started by `fabric up`, so its configuration cannot be checked
messages.fix: run `fabric up`, then `fabric verify --production`

messages.name: production_checks_passed
messages.text: every production check passed
messages.fix: none needed

messages.name: canary_tap_empty
messages.text: the canary's spans did not reach the canary tap, so delivery through the Node cannot be read back
messages.fix: read the Node's log (`docker logs` of the project's fabric-node container), then run `fabric up` again; `fabric doctor` names known errors
